# Nishaani — Community Memory Workbench

Nishaani is a local-first prototype for the careful stewardship of oral-history collections. It focuses on the work around a recording: provenance, transcript revision, access labels, exhibition drafts, and portable backups.

## Run it

This is a static site. Open `index.html` directly or deploy the folder to Vercel as a static project. No build command, environment variables, paid service, or database is required. Three.js and GSAP are loaded from public CDNs for the 3D recorder and motion; if those scripts fail, the hero falls back to an inline illustration and the core pages remain usable.

## What is real in this demo

- All seven pages and their local interactions run in the browser.
- Records, transcript edits, rights labels, exhibitions, and activity are stored in this browser's `localStorage`.
- Selected audio can be previewed in the current tab with a waveform visualization. The audio binary is not uploaded and is not included in archive backups.
- Transcript indexing suggestions are local word-frequency suggestions, not AI transcription or analysis.
- Eight fictional Thane-area records demonstrate workflows. They are not historical testimony or verified community accounts.
- Rights labels are organizational metadata, not legal consent records. Exhibition drafts are previews and are never published.

## Limits before real community use

This is not a hosted full-stack service: there is no authentication, shared database, encrypted storage, multi-user access control, server-side AI, or automatic transcription. Browser storage is device-specific and is not a secure archival backup. Obtain informed permission, establish an actual governance process, and use secure storage before importing real testimony. The product is scoped as stewardship tooling rather than as another public archive; existing regional archive initiatives already document community histories.

## Files

- `index.html` — app shell and page navigation
- `styles.css` — editorial archive visual system
- `motion.css` — motion language, responsive readability and reduced-motion support
- `app.js` — local data, page rendering and interactions
- `FEATURES.md` — capability inventory and demo boundaries

# Parley

**Real-time chat with public rooms, DMs and group chats, and a Gemini co-pilot you can @mention.** Messages, typing indicators, read receipts and reactions reach everyone live, usually in under a second. It runs entirely on Netlify: a streaming edge function for live updates, serverless functions for the API, and Netlify Blobs as the database.

**Live:** https://parley-nishant.netlify.app  ·  **Author:** [Nishant Singh](https://nishant-singhaa0240274.netlify.app)

## Features

**Chat**
- Public rooms (`#lobby`, `#ai-ml`, `#placements`, `#random`), one-to-one DMs and group chats.
- Live typing indicators, online presence, unread badges and ✓✓ read receipts in DMs and groups.
- Emoji reactions, replies with quotes, editing and deleting your own messages.
- Image and file sharing up to 4 MB: attach, paste or drag and drop, with an upload progress bar and a lightbox.
- Optimistic sending: your message appears instantly, then reconciles with the server copy.
- One-click guest accounts with random names, or sign up with a username and password.

**Gemini**
- **@gemini** in any message and Gemini replies in the thread, using the recent conversation as context.
- **Smart replies:** three suggested responses to the latest message.
- **Catch me up:** a summary and key points of what you missed.
- **Translate** any message between English and Hindi.

**Safety**
- Passwords hashed with scrypt; sessions are HS256 JWTs signed with the Web Crypto API.
- DMs and groups are readable only by their members (checked on every API call and on the live stream).
- A word filter masks common English and Hinglish abuse in public rooms.
- Per-user and per-IP rate limits on sign-ups, messages, uploads and AI calls.
- Uploaded HTML, SVG and script files are served as downloads, never rendered.

## How the live updates work

Netlify doesn't run long-lived WebSocket servers, so Parley uses **Server-Sent Events from an edge function**:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as Browser A
  participant API as Function /api/*
  participant DB as Netlify Blobs
  participant Edge as Edge function /api/live
  participant B as Browser B
  B->>Edge: EventSource (live ticket, open chat, last seq)
  A->>API: POST /api/convs/lobby/messages
  API->>DB: claim m/lobby/42 (only if new)
  API->>DB: update head/lobby (seq, preview)
  API-->>A: 201 (optimistic bubble confirmed)
  loop every 0.7 s
    Edge->>DB: read heads + inbox, probe m/lobby/43
  end
  Edge-->>B: event: head, event: messages
```

- **Ordering without a database server.** Each message is stored under its own key, `m/<chat>/<seq>`. A sender claims the next sequence number with a conditional write (`onlyIfNew`) and reads it back to confirm it won. If another sender got there first, it takes the next number. In the test suite, 40 messages sent at once by three users are all stored, with no gaps or duplicates.
- **Cheap to run.** Edge functions are billed per request, not per second. Each stream lasts 25 seconds and then reconnects, so an open tab costs about 150 stream requests an hour. Background tabs pause their stream after a minute and catch up when you come back.
- **Fallbacks.** If streaming fails three times (for example, behind a proxy that buffers responses), the app switches to polling `/api/sync` every 2 seconds, and the status in the sidebar changes to "Syncing every 2 s".
- **Edits and reactions** bump a revision number on the chat's head document; the stream then sends the changed messages.
- **DMs and groups** also fan out to each member's inbox document, which drives unread badges and makes new chats appear in the sidebar.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Browser
    UI[React UIoptimistic store] --> ES[EventSource]
  end
  UI -- "REST + JWT" --> F[Netlify Function/api/* router]
  ES -- "SSE" --> E[Edge function/api/live]
  F --> DB[(Netlify Blobsusers · chats · messagesheads · inboxes · files)]
  E --> DB
  F --> G[Gemini API]
```

| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| Frontend | React 18, Vite, Framer Motion, a small `useSyncExternalStore` store |
| Live updates | Netlify Edge Function (Deno) streaming Server-Sent Events, with a polling fallback |
| API | Netlify Functions (Node 22), one router for 24 routes |
| Database | Netlify Blobs (strong consistency, conditional writes) |
| Auth | scrypt password hashes, HS256 JWTs (Web Crypto), short-lived tickets for the stream |
| AI | Gemini API with structured JSON output and a fallback chain across models |

### Data model (Blobs keys)

| Key | Contents |
|---|---|
| `users/<id>`, `handles/<handle>` | Profile and password hash; handle claimed with `onlyIfNew` |
| `d/<handle>~<id>~…` | People directory (search reads key names only, no documents) |
| `conv/<chat>` | Room, DM or group: type, name, members |
| `head/<chat>` | Latest seq, preview, typing, read positions, edit revision |
| `m/<chat>/<seq>` | One message |
| `inbox/<user>` | A user's DMs and groups, with their read positions |
| `presence/<user>`, `file/<id>`, `limit/…` | Last seen, uploads (with metadata), rate-limit windows |

## API

All routes except auth, health and file downloads need `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

| Method | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/api/auth/signup` · `/login` · `/guest` | Create an account, sign in, or get a guest account |
| `GET` | `/api/bootstrap` | You, your chats with their heads, users, AI status |
| `PATCH` | `/api/me` | Change display name or about |
| `GET` | `/api/users?q=` | Search people |
| `POST` | `/api/convs` | Start a DM `{type:"dm", with}` or group `{type:"group", name, members}` |
| `GET` | `/api/convs/:id/messages?before=|after=` | Page through history (50 at a time) |
| `POST` | `/api/convs/:id/messages` | Send `{text, fileId?, replyTo?, cmid?}` |
| `PATCH` | `/api/convs/:id/messages/:seq` | `{react}`, `{text}` or `{delete:true}` |
| `POST` | `/api/convs/:id/typing` · `/read` | Typing indicator, read position |
| `POST` | `/api/convs/:id/ai/reply` · `/smart-replies` · `/catch-up` | Gemini features |
| `POST` | `/api/ai/translate` | `{text, to: "en" \| "hi"}` |
| `POST` / `GET` | `/api/files` · `/api/files/:id` | Upload (multipart, 4 MB) and download |
| `POST` | `/api/live-ticket` | A 10-minute ticket for the stream |
| `GET` | `/api/live?t=&c=&s=` | The live stream (edge function) |
| `GET` | `/api/sync` | Polling fallback |
| `GET` | `/api/health` | Status and configuration |

## Run it locally

```bash
npm install
npm install -g netlify-cli
netlify dev              # app + API + local Blobs at http://localhost:8888
```

Optional: put `GEMINI_API_KEY=...` in a `.env` file to turn on the AI features.

Local development streams from a Node twin of the edge function (`/api/live-node`, which returns 410 in production), because the Deno runtime for edge functions isn't always available offline. Both use the same code in `shared/live-core.js`.

With `netlify dev` running, run the API tests (39 checks: auth, permissions, concurrency, DMs, groups, reactions, edits, files, moderation, sync):

```bash
python3 tests/api_test.py
```

## Deploy (Netlify free plan)

1. Push this folder to a GitHub repository named `parley`.
2. Netlify → **Add new project → Import an existing project → GitHub** → pick `parley`. Build settings come from `netlify.toml`.
3. Before deploying, add the environment variable `GEMINI_API_KEY` and mark it as a secret.
   - Optional: `JWT_SECRET`, at least 16 characters. Without it, a random secret is generated once and kept in Blobs.
   - Optional: `ADMIN_HANDLES`, a comma-separated list of usernames that can delete any message in public rooms.
   - Optional: `GEMINI_MODEL`, a model to try before the built-in list.
4. Name the project `parley-nishant`, deploy, then click **Make public**.

## Project structure

```
shared/live-core.js       the live stream (used by the edge function and the dev twin)
shared/jwt.js             HS256 sign/verify on Web Crypto (Node + Deno)
shared/constants.js       rooms, limits, reactions
netlify/edge-functions/   live.js: SSE stream at /api/live
netlify/functions/        api.mjs (REST router), live-node.mjs (local dev only)
netlify/lib/              db (Blobs, seq claims, heads, inboxes), auth, ai, gemini, moderation
src/lib/                  store (state + optimistic updates), live (EventSource + fallback), api
src/components/           Landing, Sidebar, Chat + Composer, Message, Panels
tests/api_test.py         end-to-end API tests
```

## License

MIT © Nishant Singh

# Praxis

**A workbench of three AI agents that show their work.** Each agent plans, calls tools, and lays out every step as it runs. They're built on Gemini — but with real logic underneath (analysis, scoring, retrieval), so they keep working even when the model is offline or the free tier is busy. Switch between a warm editorial light theme and a glass-neon dark theme.

**Live:** https://praxis-nishant.netlify.app  ·  **Author:** [Nishant Singh](https://nishant-singhaa0240274.netlify.app)

## The three agents

Each is a different agent *pattern*, so together they show range:

### Data-analysis agent — *plan → act → observe*
Paste a CSV, ask in plain English. It reads the data and infers column types, **plans** which operation answers the question, **runs the computation**, and **writes the finding** with a chart. The planning and computation are deterministic; the model only writes the two-sentence narrative.

### Career agent — *generate → critique → iterate*
Paste a job description and your resume. It extracts the required skills, scores your resume against them (an **ATS-style keyword match**, with matched/missing shown), then tailors bullets to close the gaps.

### Research agent — *retrieve → synthesize → cite*
Paste sources and ask a question. It chunks them, **retrieves** the most relevant passages with **TF-IDF cosine similarity**, and synthesizes a **cited** answer. Real RAG retrieval, no embeddings service required.

## Why "shows its work"

Every agent renders its plan and tool calls as a live trace — `parse_csv`, `reason`, `compute`, `tf-idf`, `ats_match`, `gemini` — so you can see it *think*, not just answer. That's the difference between an agent and a chatbot.

## The model layer is optional

The browser does the real work (parsing, planning, scoring, retrieval). The backend is one thin Netlify Function (`/api/generate`) that proxies Gemini for the written layer. If `GEMINI_API_KEY` is unset, the free tier is busy, or the call fails, each agent falls back to a deterministic version and tags the output `offline`. **The demo always works.**

## Theming

One design system, two themes, toggled live and remembered per visitor:
- **Light** — warm editorial: Fraunces italic display, paper tones, amber accents.
- **Dark** — glass-neon: Space Grotesk, an animated aurora, translucent glass panels.

## Tech stack

TypeScript everywhere · React 18 + Vite · Netlify Functions (Node 22) · Gemini (free tier, optional) · hand-built SVG charts · no UI or charting library.

## What it demonstrates

Gen-AI and ML coursework put into working agents: the agentic plan/act loop, RAG retrieval, prompt design with graceful fallback, and real client-side ML-adjacent logic (TF-IDF, keyword scoring, data analysis) — from the Stanford/DeepLearning.AI ML Specialization, IBM Data Science, Google & AWS Gen-AI, and Cisco "Apply AI" tracks.

## Run it

```bash
npm install
npm run build
npx netlify dev          # http://localhost:8888
```

| Variable | Required | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | No | Turns on the model-written layer (free tier, no billing). Without it, every agent uses its deterministic fallback. |

## Tests

```bash
npm test          # 37 checks
npm run typecheck # strict TypeScript
```

- **Data** — CSV parsing and type inference, rule-based planning, aggregation/top-N/summary/trend, the deterministic narrative.
- **Career** — keyword extraction, ATS-style scoring (a strong resume scores high, an off-target one low), gap detection.
- **Research** — chunking and TF-IDF retrieval ranking the right passage first.
- **Backend** — the endpoint degrades to `fallback` with no key.

CI runs typecheck, tests and build on every push.

## Deploy on Netlify

Build command `npm run build`, publish directory `dist`. The function is auto-detected. Optionally add `GEMINI_API_KEY` under Site settings → Environment variables (free tier is fine; no billing needed).

## License

MIT © 2026 Nishant Singh.

# Privacy Prism

Privacy Prism is a free, browser-only synthetic-data release-readiness lab. It compares an original/reference CSV with a synthetic CSV and turns the results into readable evidence for a human review. The selected visual direction is the dark **Privacy Prism** concept: graphite panels, large readable typography, a sharply faceted vector crystal, animated light dispersion, and pointer-responsive tilt.

## Start

Open `index.html` directly, or serve this folder locally:

```sh
python3 -m http.server 8000
```

Visit `http://localhost:8000`. No build step, package installation, account, API key, or paid service is required. Google Fonts improve the visual match; the design falls back to system fonts if they are unavailable.

## Deploy on Vercel

1. Upload the contents of this folder to the root of a GitHub repository.
2. Import the repository in Vercel.
3. Choose **Other** as the framework preset, leave the build command empty, and set the output directory to `.`.
4. Deploy.

## Preserved core features

- **Utility and fidelity:** compare numeric distributions with a two-sample empirical CDF distance plus standardized mean movement; compare categories with total variation distance.
- **Nearest-row similarity screen:** compare up to 250 synthetic rows against up to 250 source rows using normalized, shared non-identifier fields; report exact overlaps and mean nearest-row similarity.
- **Group coverage:** compare proportions for one selected categorical field and inspect missing categories.

## Ten added checks and workflows

1. **Schema alignment:** find source-only and synthetic-only columns.
2. **Missingness fidelity:** compare per-field null rates.
3. **Distribution-shape screen:** report KS distance for numeric fields and total variation distance for categories.
4. **Relationship drift:** compare pairwise Pearson correlations for numeric feature pairs.
5. **Range and category validity:** identify numeric values outside the source range and categories not observed in the source.
6. **Record integrity:** count duplicate rows in both datasets.
7. **Attribute-inference scenario:** choose known fields and a sensitive field to see whether synthetic groups can help predict source values, with a majority baseline.
8. **Intersectional coverage:** compare two-field combinations to find source combinations absent from synthetic data.
9. **Downstream model utility proxy:** compare a simple 1-nearest-neighbor classifier trained on source versus synthetic rows, evaluated on held-out source rows.
10. **User-defined release gate and evidence pack:** set thresholds, see PASS / REVIEW / HOLD flags, and download aggregate JSON evidence.

Every analysis control is functional in the browser. The included customer-style demo data is fabricated for interface exploration and contains no real people.

## Privacy and interpretation

CSV files are parsed in browser memory. The app does not send rows to a server or include rows in the JSON evidence export. It does not save uploaded data in local storage; closing the tab clears it. The optional theme preference is stored locally.

These are exploratory screens, not a certification, legal assessment, differential-privacy guarantee, or proof against re-identification. Nearest-neighbor similarity is not a probability of disclosure. The inference and model checks are deliberately simple and can be unstable on small data. Range validity can flag legitimate generated tail values. A passing user-defined gate is not evidence that data is safe to publish. Review the in-app **Method & limitations** page and get an appropriate privacy/security review before releasing sensitive data.

## Product position

The problem is real and active: teams need an understandable release review that examines utility, similarity risk signals, missingness, relationships, and subgroup blind spots together. This project should be presented as a distinctive local-first workflow and visual product experience—not as a claim that synthetic-data evaluation is a wholly untouched research area.

# PrivateLedger

**On-device personal finance intelligence. Your money never leaves your machine.**

PrivateLedger reads your bank statements, categorises every transaction, answers questions about your spending, forecasts your cash flow, and scans receipts — and it does all of it **locally in your browser**. No account, no server, no upload. The language model itself runs on your device via WebGPU.

> Most finance apps send your statements to their servers. PrivateLedger has no server to breach, subpoena, or sell to — the whole pipeline runs on your machine.

## Live Demo: https://private-ledger-nishant.netlify.app/

---

## Table of contents

- [What it does](#what-it-does)
- [Why it's different](#why-its-different)
- [How it works](#how-it-works)
- [Tech stack](#tech-stack)
- [Project structure](#project-structure)
- [Running locally](#running-locally)
- [Deploying to Netlify](#deploying-to-netlify)
- [The Free / Pro model](#the-free--pro-model)
- [Configuration](#configuration)
- [Browser support](#browser-support)
- [Privacy](#privacy)
- [Roadmap](#roadmap)
- [Disclaimers](#disclaimers)

---

## What it does

| Feature | What it does | Free limit (per day) | Pro |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Import** | Reads `.csv` and `.pdf` bank statements, parsed entirely in the browser | Unlimited | Unlimited |
| **Auto-categorise** | Sorts every transaction into categories (Food, Transport, Bills…) | Unlimited | Unlimited |
| **Dashboard** | Money in / out / net, top category, a spend-by-category chart, full transaction table | Unlimited | Unlimited |
| **Ask** | Natural-language questions answered from your own numbers, by an on-device LLM | 5 | Unlimited |
| **Forecast** | Projects next month's spend per category from your recent averages | 2 | Unlimited |
| **Receipt scan** | On-device OCR of a receipt photo → extracts the total → adds a transaction | 3 | Unlimited |
| **Tax assistant** | General India tax guidance grounded in built-in reference notes | 3 | Unlimited |

Every feature is fully built and available in the free tier — Pro only lifts the daily caps and loads a larger model. Limits reset daily and are tracked in `localStorage`.

---

## Why it's different

Existing finance apps (Mint-style trackers and newer AI tools) upload your financial data to the cloud to analyse it. That creates a permanent privacy liability — a breach, a data-sharing deal, or a subpoena can expose your entire financial life.

PrivateLedger takes the opposite approach: **the intelligence comes to your data, not the other way around.** Parsing, categorisation, the language model, OCR, and forecasting all execute client-side. The privacy promise isn't a policy you have to trust — it's enforced by the architecture.

---

## How it works

```
  Your statement (CSV / PDF)
            │
            ▼
   ┌─────────────────┐     all in the browser
   │  Parse locally  │     (pdf.js / CSV parser)
   └───────┬─────────┘
           ▼
   ┌─────────────────┐
   │   Categorise    │     keyword rules → category per transaction
   └───────┬─────────┘
           ▼
   ┌─────────────────┐
   │   Dashboard     │     tiles + doughnut chart + table (Chart.js)
   └───────┬─────────┘
           ▼
   ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │  Ask / Tax      →  on-device LLM (WebLLM/WebGPU) │
   │  Forecast       →  pure-JS projection            │
   │  Receipt scan   →  on-device OCR (Tesseract.js)  │
   └───────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Retrieval for the chat:** when you ask a question, PrivateLedger computes a compact summary of your data locally (totals, per-category spend, largest transactions, date range) and passes only that summary to the on-device model as grounding. The model answers from your real numbers rather than guessing.

---

## Tech stack

- **Plain HTML / CSS / JavaScript** — no build step, no framework. Two static files.
- **[WebLLM](https://github.com/mlc-ai/web-llm)** (`@mlc-ai/web-llm`) — runs a quantized small language model in-browser via **WebGPU**. Default model: `Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct` (Pro uses `Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct`).
- **[pdf.js](https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/)** — extracts text from PDF statements.
- **[Chart.js](https://www.chartjs.org/)** — the spending chart.
- **[Tesseract.js](https://tesseract.projectnaptha.com/)** — on-device OCR for receipts.
- **Google Fonts** — Plus Jakarta Sans + Space Mono.

All libraries load from public CDNs. There is **no backend and no API key** anywhere in this project.

---

## Project structure

```
privateledger/
├── index.html    # Landing page (Tactile 3D design, animated hero, pricing)
├── app.html      # The full application (import, dashboard, ask, forecast, receipts, tax)
└── README.md
```

That's the whole app. Static files, nothing to compile.

---

## Running locally

Because the app uses ES modules and `fetch`, open it through a local server rather than double-clicking the file.

```bash
# from the project folder, pick any one:
python3 -m http.server 8000
# or
npx serve .
```

Then visit `http://localhost:8000` (landing) and `http://localhost:8000/app.html` (the app).

> The on-device model and OCR download model/engine files on first use. Give the first chat a minute — after that everything is cached in your browser.

---

## Deploying to Netlify

1. Push `index.html`, `app.html`, and `README.md` to a GitHub repo.
2. In Netlify: **Add new site → Import an existing project → GitHub** → select the repo.
3. Leave **build command** and **publish directory** empty — it's a static site.
4. Deploy. Your site is live at `https://<your-site>.netlify.app/`, and the app at `/app.html`.

Every push to the repo redeploys automatically.

---

## The Free / Pro model

The free tier includes every feature, each capped per day. **Pro** removes the caps and loads a larger model. Unlocking is done with a secret code (no payment integration in this version) — the "paid" features are fully present in the code and gated behind a flag, so a real payment step can be added later without touching the feature code.

- Enter the code via the **Unlock Pro** button.
- Default code: `LEDGER-PRO-2026` (change it — see below).
- The unlock state is stored in `localStorage` on the user's device.

---

## Configuration

All settings live in one `CONFIG` object near the top of the `<script>` in **`app.html`**:

```js
const CONFIG = {
  PRO_CODE: "LEDGER-PRO-2026",          // your secret Pro unlock code
  MODEL: "Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-q4f16_1-MLC",   // free-tier model
  WEBLLM_URL: "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@mlc-ai/web-llm@0.2.79/+esm",
  TESSERACT_URL: "https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/tesseract.js/5.1.1/tesseract.min.js",
  LIMITS: { ask: 5, forecast: 2, receipt: 3, tax: 3 }   // free daily caps
};
```

- **Change the Pro code** → edit `PRO_CODE`.
- **Change daily limits** → edit `LIMITS`.
- **Use a different / smaller model** → change `MODEL` to any ID from WebLLM's prebuilt list (smaller = faster download, less capable).

---

## Browser support

| Feature | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Import, categorise, dashboard, forecast | Any modern browser |
| Receipt OCR | Any modern browser (uses WebAssembly) |
| Ask + Tax assistant (the LLM) | **Chrome or Edge on desktop** with WebGPU |

The app detects missing WebGPU and shows a friendly "open in Chrome/Edge" message rather than failing silently. First model load downloads roughly 0.9 GB (free model), cached afterwards.

---

## Privacy

- Files are parsed in the browser and **never transmitted**.
- The language model runs locally — **no API calls, no logging**.
- OCR runs locally.
- The app works **offline** once the model and libraries are cached.
- There is no analytics, no tracking, and no server in this project.

---

## Roadmap

- Point the landing-page CTAs directly at `/app.html`.
- Persist imported transactions locally (IndexedDB) so they survive a refresh.
- Smarter PDF statement parsing for more bank formats.
- Optional Stripe **test-mode** checkout in place of the unlock code.
- Budgets and recurring-payment detection.

---

## Disclaimers

PrivateLedger is a demo project. It does **not** provide financial or investment advice. The tax assistant gives **general information only**, grounded in illustrative reference notes that may not reflect the current financial year — always verify with a qualified professional. Statement parsing is best-effort and should be checked against your actual statements.

---

*Built to run entirely on your device. Your data never leaves your machine.*

Build good habits, quit the ones you don't want, hit quantity goals, keep streaks, track mood, earn XP and achievements, and see your consistency in a year heatmap — all offline. Tracking — build & quit habits, quantity goals, custom units, daily / X-per-week / pick-days schedules, one-tap check, quantity stepper, progress ring, backfill any day, rest/skip days, per-habit color & SVG icon, tags, reminders, notes.

Streaks & stats — current & best streak, 7/30/all-time rates, weekly goal tracking, at-risk alerts, perfect-day detection, year heatmap, 8-week chart, best-weekday insight, per-habit consistency bars.

Gamification & review — XP, levels, progress bar, 8 achievements, per-day notes, 5-point mood logging.

Coach & data — offline smart coach, optional Gemini coach, JSON backup/restore, CSV export, progress-card copy, reset.

# QuickResume

**An AI resume builder that shows its work.** Gemini drafts and sharpens your resume, a live preview shows exactly what the PDF will look like, and a transparent ATS score tells you how the resume reads against any job description: which keywords are missing, which bullets have no numbers, and what to fix first. Then practise the interview with questions written for your resume.

**Live:** https://quickresume-nishant.netlify.app  ·  **Author:** [Nishant Singh](https://nishant-singhaa0240274.netlify.app)

## Features

**Write**
- **Import** an existing resume (PDF, image or pasted text). Gemini reads it into structured, editable sections and keeps your wording.
- **Draft from notes:** rough notes about your education, internships and projects become a complete first draft.
- **One-click rewrites** for any bullet: stronger, add impact, shorter, or use the job's keywords. You pick from three options.
- **No invented facts:** the AI is told never to make up employers, tools or numbers. Where a metric would help, it leaves a highlighted `[placeholder]`, and the ATS check reminds you to fill it in.
- A live **bullet checker** (green, amber or orange dot) flags weak openers like "Responsible for…" and bullets without a measurable result.

**Check**
- **ATS score out of 100**, recomputed as you type, with a breakdown: keyword match (40), impact (20), completeness (15), role fit (10), length and readability (10), structure (5).
- **Keywords** from the job description, split into must-haves and nice-to-haves, and marked as found in your bullets, only in your skills list, or missing. Gemini can read the job description too and add keywords the built-in dictionary doesn't know.
- **Prioritised tips**: click one to jump to the exact bullet.
- **Tailor to this job:** Gemini suggests a new summary and rewrites of the bullets that match the job. You accept each change, and every change can be undone.

**Present**
- Three **ATS-safe templates** (Modern, Classic, Technical): single column, real text, standard headings, accent colours, text size and spacing controls, A4 or US Letter.
- **PDF download** through the browser's print engine. The output was checked with `pdftotext`: selectable text, embedded TrueType fonts and one page for the example resume.
- **Public link** (`/r/your-name-xxxx`) with a view counter, **private edit link** to continue on another device, plain-text copy for job portals, and JSON backup.

**Practise**
- **Interview questions** written for your resume and the job: technical, project deep-dives, role scenarios and behavioural.
- Type an answer and get a **score out of 10**, what worked, what to improve and a stronger version.
- Works without AI too, using a built-in bank of questions matched to your skills.

## How the ATS score works

The score is deterministic TypeScript in `shared/ats.ts`. It runs in the browser on every keystroke and on the server through `POST /api/ats`.

1. **Reading the job description.** A dictionary of over 200 skills with their common spellings (`shared/skills.ts`) finds keywords such as "Node.js / nodejs / node js". Words that are also plain English only count when they look like the skill, so "react quickly" is not React and "go-live" is not Go. Lines under "Nice to have" or "Preferred" headings make a keyword optional. Soft skills weigh less. Repeated two-word phrases catch domain terms ("payment systems"). The job title, years of experience and degree are extracted too.
2. **Scoring the resume.** A keyword found in a bullet or the summary earns full credit. One found only in the skills list earns 75%, because recruiters look for proof. Bullets are checked for an action verb and a number. The remaining parts check contact details, length (one page for early-career resumes) and standard section headings.
3. **Tips** are generated from the gaps and sorted by impact.

The engine has its own unit tests (`npm test`).

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Browser
    E[EditorReact + immer store] --> A[ATS engineshared/ats.ts]
    E --> P[Live previewResumeView]
    P --> PDF[Print to PDF]
  end
  E -- "autosave (x-edit-key)" --> F[Netlify Function/api/* router]
  F --> B[(Netlify Blobsresumes · public links · rate limits)]
  F --> G[Gemini APIstructured JSON output]
  F --> A2[Same ATS engineserver-side]
  C[Scheduled functiondaily cleanup] --> B
```

| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| Frontend | React 18, **TypeScript**, Vite, React Router, Framer Motion, immer (undo/redo) |
| Backend | Netlify Functions (TypeScript, Node 22): one router, plus a daily scheduled cleanup |
| Database | Netlify Blobs: resumes, public links (claimed with `onlyIfNew`), view counts and rate limits |
| AI | Gemini API with JSON schemas, PDF/image input, a model fallback chain and per-IP limits |
| Shared code | `shared/`: the resume model, validation, the ATS engine, skills dictionary and question bank, used by both browser and server |

**Privacy by design:** there are no accounts. Creating a resume returns a random edit key that stays in your browser (only its SHA-256 hash is stored). The private edit link carries the key in the URL fragment (`#k=…`), which browsers never send to servers. Job descriptions stay in your browser. Resumes that are never shared and not edited for 180 days are deleted by the cleanup job.

## API

| Method | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/api/resumes` | Create a resume → `{ id, key }` |
| `GET` / `PUT` / `DELETE` | `/api/resumes/:id` | Read, save or delete (header `x-edit-key`) |
| `POST` | `/api/resumes/list` | Titles and dates for the resumes this browser has keys for |
| `POST` / `DELETE` | `/api/resumes/:id/publish` | Create or remove the public link |
| `GET` | `/api/public/:slug` | A shared resume (counts one view per visitor every 6 hours) |
| `POST` | `/api/ats` | `{ resume, jd, ai? }` → score, parts, keywords and tips |
| `POST` | `/api/ai/import` | `{ text }` or `{ file: { mimeType, data } }` → structured resume |
| `POST` | `/api/ai/draft` | Notes → first draft |
| `POST` | `/api/ai/bullet` | `{ text, mode: improve \| quantify \| shorten \| keywords }` → 3 options |
| `POST` | `/api/ai/summary` · `/api/ai/keywords` · `/api/ai/tailor` | Summary options, job keywords, tailoring suggestions |
| `POST` | `/api/ai/interview` · `/api/ai/feedback` | Questions (AI or built-in bank) and answer feedback |
| `GET` | `/api/health` | Status and configuration |

## Run it locally

```bash
npm install
npm install -g netlify-cli
netlify dev              # app + API + local Blobs at http://localhost:8888
```

Optional: put `GEMINI_API_KEY=...` in a `.env` file to turn on the AI features. Without it, everything else works: the editor, templates, PDF, ATS score and the built-in interview questions.

Tests:

```bash
npm test                  # ATS engine unit tests (Node 22)
npm run typecheck         # TypeScript, strict mode
python3 tests/api_test.py # 30 end-to-end API checks (needs netlify dev running)
```

## Deploy (Netlify free plan)

1. Push this folder to a GitHub repository named `quickresume`.
2. Netlify → **Add new project → Import an existing project → GitHub** → pick `quickresume`. Build settings come from `netlify.toml`.
3. Before deploying, add the environment variable `GEMINI_API_KEY` and mark it as a secret. Optional: `GEMINI_MODEL`, a model to try before the built-in list.
4. Name the project `quickresume-nishant`, deploy, then click **Make public**.

## Project structure

```
shared/types.ts        the resume model
shared/normalize.ts    validates any incoming JSON into a safe Resume
shared/ats.ts          job-description analysis and scoring
shared/skills.ts       skills dictionary with spellings and case rules
shared/verbs.ts        action verbs, weak openers, bullet checks
shared/questions.ts    built-in interview question bank
netlify/functions/     api.mts (router), cleanup.mts (daily)
netlify/lib/           Blobs storage, Gemini client, prompts, HTTP helpers
src/pages/             Landing, Start, Editor, PublicResume
src/editor/            Content, Design, ATS and Interview panels
src/resume/            the three templates, preview and pagination
tests/                 ATS unit tests, API tests
```

# SHIFT — Factory Twin

An interactive digital-factory scheduling simulator. Inject a machine outage, rush order, or supplier delay, compare the baseline with a recovery plan, and see the projected trade-offs across throughput, recovery time, idle time, and on-time orders.

## Run it free

Open `index.html` in a modern browser. The core simulation runs locally in the browser. It needs no account, API key, database, or paid service.

## Publish with GitHub and Netlify

1. Extract `SHIFT-Factory-Twin-Netlify.zip` on your computer.
2. Create a GitHub repository and upload the extracted project files and folders to the repository root. Upload `index.html`, `styles.css`, `app.js`, `netlify.toml`, and the `netlify/` folder. Do not upload only the ZIP as the repository contents.
3. In Netlify, select **Add new project → Import an existing project**, connect GitHub, and choose the repository.
4. Keep the settings in `netlify.toml`: publish directory `.` and no build command. Deploy.

The base site requires no environment variables. The Netlify Function in `netlify/functions/premium-plan.js` is a dormant optional extension. It only calls a model if you deliberately configure all three Netlify environment variables: `MODEL_API_URL`, `MODEL_API_KEY`, and `MODEL_NAME`. The endpoint must use an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions request format. Without those settings, the function returns a locked response and makes no external request. The website's premium card is informational; it does not trigger paid calls.

## What works in the free demo

- Animated isometric factory floor with machine states, job flow, zoom, and simulation clock controls.
- Three injectable disruption scenarios: machine outage, rush order, and supplier delay.
- A deterministic local scheduler proposal with an ordered recovery sequence.
- Baseline/recovery comparisons, a production timeline, and outcome metrics.
- Responsive layout, keyboard-usable dialogs, and reduced-motion support.

## Scope and honesty

This is a simulated digital twin, not connected factory-control software. Machines, jobs, disruptions, forecasts, and all performance figures are illustrative. The free planner uses deterministic scenario rules, not an AI agent. The premium Netlify Function is an optional connector for a paid model endpoint; it returns proposals for human review and never executes factory changes.

## Files

- `index.html` — application shell, simulator, timeline, metrics, and dialogs
- `styles.css` — responsive control-room visual design and animation
- `app.js` — local scenario state and recovery simulation
- `netlify.toml` — Netlify publish and function settings
- `netlify/functions/premium-plan.js` — optional, locked paid-model connector

# Salarium

**What should a software developer earn?** Salarium gives an honest answer: an estimate *and* the range where 80% of similar developers actually land, the reasons behind the number (SHAP), how it grows with experience, which skills go with higher pay, and an AI check of real job offers. It's trained on 17,332 real salaries from the Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025 across 59 countries, and shows every country in its own currency (Indian pay in lakhs per year).

**Live:** https://salarium-nishant.netlify.app  ·  **Author:** [Nishant Singh](https://nishant-singhaa0240274.netlify.app)

## Features

- **Estimate with a range.** A LightGBM model predicts total yearly pay; two quantile models, calibrated with conformal prediction, give the 80% range. It's in local currency, with the country median marked for comparison.
- **What moves your number.** Exact SHAP values for every estimate: how much your country, experience, role, company size, work setup and each technology raise or lower pay compared with the average developer in the data.
- **Your next 30 years.** The same profile at every level of experience, with the range as a band. A monotone constraint means more experience never lowers the estimate.
- **What-ifs.** The technologies most linked to higher pay for *your* profile (add one with a click and the estimate updates), and the same profile in every other role.
- **Market data.** Median pay by country (middle half shown), pay by experience for any country, and pay premiums for 103 technologies, roles and work setups, **controlling for country and experience**, with 95% confidence intervals.
- **Model card.** Test-set accuracy against simpler baselines, range calibration, accuracy by country, feature importance, every data-cleaning step, method and limits.
- **Offer check (Gemini).** Paste an offer letter or upload a PDF or image. Gemini extracts fixed pay, variable pay, equity, benefits and joining bonus (it understands Indian CTC and "LPA"). Salarium converts it to a like-for-like yearly total, places it in your range with an approximate percentile, and writes talking points and a negotiation email. You can also type the numbers without AI.
- **Real-world accuracy.** Visitors can anonymously check an estimate against their actual pay (rounded to $500, no identity stored). The model page shows the live score next to the test-set score.
- **Save & share.** Shareable report links (`/r/…`) that recompute the estimate on view.

## The model

| Model (test set, 2,600 people) | Typical error (MdAPE) | R² (log pay) | Within ±25% |
|---|---|---|---|
| Global median | ±42.6% | –0.03 | 32% |
| Country median | ±30.2% | 0.54 | 43% |
| Ridge regression | ±23.2% | 0.69 | 53% |
| **LightGBM** | **±21.6%** | **0.70** | **56%** |

- **80% range coverage:** the raw quantile models covered 72.3% of real salaries. After **conformalized quantile regression** on a separate calibration set, the range covers **81.3%** of the test set.
- **India:** ±34% typical error on 128 Indian test cases, versus ±66% for the country median alone.
- Salary data is noisy: two people with identical answers can earn very different amounts. That's why the site reports typical error and a calibrated range rather than an "accuracy" percentage.

**Pipeline** (`python/`)
1. `download.py` fetches the survey (141 MB) from Stack Overflow's official archive.
2. `prepare.py` keeps professional developers who are employed or self-employed and reported pay, then removes outliers **within each country** (Tukey's fences on log pay, which catch monthly salaries typed into the yearly box). Countries need at least 30 clean responses. The result: 49,191 → 17,332 responses, 59 countries and 104 technologies. Local currencies use the exchange rates implied by the survey itself.
3. `train.py` uses a 70 / 15 / 15 train / calibration / test split, stratified by country. It trains the baselines, the ridge model (one-hot + splines) and LightGBM with native categorical splits and a monotone constraint on experience; settings come from 5-fold cross-validation on the training set only. It then fits the quantile models and conformal adjustment, computes SHAP importance and the market analysis, and exports everything.

**Serving without Python.** The trees are exported to `netlify/model/model.js` and evaluated by a small TypeScript runtime (`shared/model.ts`), which also implements **exact TreeSHAP** (Lundberg et al., 2018). `tests/parity.test.ts` checks it against LightGBM on 300 test rows: predictions and SHAP values match to within 1e-8.

Features: country, years of experience, years coding, role, education, company size, IC or manager, work setup, industry, employment type and 103 technologies. **Age and gender are deliberately not used.**

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Offline
    S[(Stack Overflow survey 2025)] --> P[prepare.pycleaning + features] --> T[train.pyLightGBM + quantiles + conformal]
    T --> M[model.js1,185 trees]
    T --> J[market.json · model-card.json · features.json]
  end
  subgraph Netlify
    W[React + TypeScript app] --> F["Functions: /api/estimate · /api/reports · /api/reality · /api/offer · /api/health"]
    F --> R[TypeScript tree runtime + TreeSHAP]
    M --> R
    F --> B[(Netlify Blobsreports · real-world checks · counters · rate limits)]
    F --> G[Gemini APIoffer reading]
    J --> W
  end
```

### API

| Method | Path | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/estimate` | Profile → range (USD), SHAP drivers, 0–30 year curve, skill and role what-ifs |
| POST | `/api/reports` | Save a profile, get a share id |
| GET | `/api/reports/:id` | A saved report with a freshly computed estimate |
| POST | `/api/reality` | Compare actual pay with the estimate (anonymous) |
| GET | `/api/reality` | Live real-world accuracy |
| POST | `/api/offer` | Offer text, file or numbers → like-for-like total, percentile, advice |
| GET | `/api/health` | Model info, AI status, usage counters |

```bash
curl -X POST https://salarium-nishant.netlify.app/api/estimate \
  -H "content-type: application/json" --data @- <<'EOF'
{ "country": "India", "yearsPro": 3, "role": "Back-end developer",
  "education": "Bachelor's degree", "orgSize": "1,000–4,999",
  "manager": "Individual contributor", "remote": "Hybrid, mostly office",
  "industry": "Software", "employment": "Employee",
  "skills": ["lang_java", "web_spring_boot", "plat_docker"] }
EOF
```

## Tech stack

Python (pandas, scikit-learn, LightGBM) for training · TypeScript everywhere else · React 18 + Vite · Framer Motion · Netlify Functions (Node 22) · Zod · Netlify Blobs · Gemini API (structured JSON output, PDF and image input) · hand-built SVG charts with tooltips and table views.

Design: International Typographic (Swiss) style. White paper, black type, one red, a visible 12-column grid, huge numerals; Inter Tight throughout. Blue marks what raises pay and red what lowers it.

## Run it yourself

```bash
npm install
npx netlify dev                          # http://localhost:8888 (uses the committed model)
```

Retrain from scratch:

```bash
pip install -r python/requirements.txt
python python/download.py && python python/prepare.py && python python/train.py
npm test                                 # parity + estimate checks
```

Deploy on Netlify (build `npm run build`, publish `dist`). The only environment variable is **`GEMINI_API_KEY`** (optional, used for reading offers); add it before the first deploy. `GEMINI_MODEL` can override the model.

## Tests

- `npm test`: the TypeScript runtime against LightGBM (predictions and SHAP), plus estimate sanity checks (ordering, monotone curve, SHAP values that add up, speed).
- `python3 tests/api_test.py`: 28 end-to-end API checks against a local server with a mock Gemini (`tests/mock_gemini.py`), covering validation, reports, anonymous reality checks and rate limits, and offers by text, file and numbers.
- `npm run typecheck`: strict TypeScript.

## Limits

- Stack Overflow survey respondents aren't a random sample of developers. In India especially, they lean towards people working for foreign companies.
- Pay was reported in mid-2025 and isn't adjusted for inflation since.
- Skill premiums are correlations, not causes.

## Data & license

Code: MIT © 2026 Nishant Singh.
Data: [Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/), made available under the [Open Database License (ODbL 1.0)](https://opendatacommons.org/licenses/odbl/1-0/). The model and statistics on this site are produced works based on that database. The raw survey isn't included in this repository; `python/download.py` fetches it.

# Tessera

**A working zero-trust access gateway.** Tessera brokers every request to every app through a single guarded gate. On each request it verifies who you are, the device and network you're on, where you're going and how sensitive it is, then **allows, challenges (step-up), or denies** — and writes the decision to a tamper-evident log. It's a live demo you can sign into as five different people and watch least-privilege access enforced in real time.

**Live:** https://tessera-nishant.netlify.app  ·  **Author:** [Nishant Singh](https://nishant-singhaa0240274.netlify.app)

## The idea

Old security trusted anything inside the network perimeter. Zero trust removes the perimeter: **never trust, always verify** — every request is authenticated, authorised and inspected, no matter where it comes from. Tessera is that model as running code, built around the **seven elements of a zero-trust architecture**:

1. **Verify identity** — who is connecting
2. **Assess access context** — the device posture and network
3. **Identify destination** — the resource and its classification
4. **Assess risk** — an adaptive score from the live signals
5. **Prevent compromise** — hard device rules and step-up re-verification
6. **Prevent data loss** — clearance vs classification, with field-level redaction
7. **Enforce policy** — a default-deny, least-privilege verdict

## Try it

Sign in as any sandbox persona (the 2FA code auto-fills for the demo). Shared password: `Sandbox#2026`.

| Persona | Role | Clearance | What they can reach |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nishant Singh | Security admin | Restricted | Everything, plus the admin console and audit trail |
| Rohan Desai | Finance | Restricted | Payroll in full — on a managed device |
| Priya Menon | People / HR | Confidential | Benefits and names, but **not** bank details |
| Meera Iyer | Engineering | Internal | The wiki; blocked from finance and HR |
| Arjun Rao | External vendor | Public | Only the public handbook |

**Things to try:** open the payroll register as the vendor (denied), then as finance (allowed). In the workspace, flip your device to *unmanaged* and watch a clean allow turn into a step-up or a block. Request just-in-time access to something you're denied, approve it as the admin, and reach it under a time-boxed grant.

## Features

- **Real authentication** — passwords hashed with PBKDF2-SHA-256 (210k iterations), RFC 6238 TOTP two-factor, and **WebAuthn passkeys** for phishing-resistant sign-in.
- **The seven-element policy engine** — pure, unit-tested decision logic returning allow / step-up / deny with a reason for every element.
- **Least privilege + data-loss prevention** — resources carry a classification and department scope; fields above your clearance are **redacted, not returned**; restricted data demands a managed device.
- **Adaptive step-up** — elevated risk or weak auth triggers re-verification; a managed-device rule or insufficient clearance can't be stepped past.
- **Just-in-time access** — request elevation, an admin grants it, and it **expires on its own** (15 minutes).
- **East-West microsegmentation** — a default-deny matrix of which workloads may talk to which, so a foothold can't pivot.
- **Tamper-evident audit** — every decision is **hash-chained** to the last; an integrity check recomputes the chain and pinpoints any alteration.
- **Encryption at rest** — TOTP seeds sealed with AES-256-GCM.
- **Brute-force protection** — failed-login lockout with escalating backoff.
- **Compliance posture** — resources mapped to NIST CSF, SOC 2, HIPAA, PCI-DSS and GDPR.
- **Hardened delivery** — strict Content-Security-Policy and security headers.

## Architecture

```
Browser (React) ──▶ /api/*  (the gate — one Netlify Function)
                      │
                      ├─ auth: PBKDF2 password · TOTP · WebAuthn passkeys
                      ├─ policy engine: the 7 elements, default-deny
                      ├─ resources: classification, scope, field redaction
                      ├─ JIT grants · East-West segmentation
                      └─ audit: AES-256-GCM at rest · SHA-256 hash chain
                      │
                   Netlify Blobs  (users, sessions, audit, grants, passkeys)
```

Everything enters through one function. There is no other path to a resource — the single brokered gate is the whole point.

### API

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/login` · `/api/verify` | Password step, then TOTP; issues a signed, HttpOnly session |
| POST | `/api/passkey/*` | WebAuthn registration and authentication |
| GET | `/api/resources` | The catalogue the signed-in user may see |
| POST | `/api/access` · `/api/stepup` | Run the policy engine; return the record or a step-up |
| GET | `/api/segmentation` | Workloads and the allowed-flow matrix |
| GET/POST | `/api/requests` · `/api/requests/decide` | Just-in-time access requests and approvals |
| GET/POST/DELETE | `/api/users` | Admin: manage sandbox users |
| GET | `/api/audit` · `/api/audit/verify` | The hash-chained log and its integrity check |

## Tech stack

TypeScript everywhere · React 18 + Vite · Netlify Functions (Node 22) · Netlify Blobs · `@simplewebauthn` · Node `crypto` (PBKDF2, AES-256-GCM, HMAC) · hand-built SVG · GitHub Actions. No UI framework — the design system is hand-written.

## What it demonstrates

Tessera puts these certifications into running code:

- **Zscaler** — the seven elements (Mastering the Fundamentals of Zero Trust, ZTCA); the gateway/exchange model, multi-cloud workload tagging and East-West segmentation (Zero Trust Cloud, EDU-240); clearance-based DLP (Data Security / Endpoint DLP, EDU-220/222); the audit trail (Security Operations, EDU-250); secure protocols (Networking for Cyber Professionals, EDU-101); policy administration (Administrator, EDU-200).
- **Google Cloud Cybersecurity Certificate** — AAA: authentication, authorization, auditing (course 3); the security lifecycle and least privilege (course 1); compliance frameworks (course 2); logging and alert monitoring (course 4).
- **Fortinet FCF** — access control and secure network architecture.

It also goes past the courses: passkeys, a hash-chained audit log, AES-256-GCM at rest, brute-force lockout, just-in-time access and a strict CSP.

> **A deliberate boundary.** Tessera only builds the defences. It does not simulate attacks, run intrusions, or set traps — the strength is shown by the gate holding and refusing the wrong request, not by attacking it.

## Run it

```bash
npm install
npm run build
npx netlify dev          # http://localhost:8888
```

No configuration is required to run. Optional environment variables:

| Variable | Required | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `TESSERA_KEY` | No | Server key for encryption at rest. A development default is used if unset — **set it in production.** |

## Tests

```bash
npm test          # 51 unit checks + 20 end-to-end checks
npm run typecheck # strict TypeScript
```

- **Unit** (`tests/run.ts`): the policy engine (least privilege, DLP, step-up, redaction, JIT), PBKDF2 round-trips, **RFC 6238 TOTP test vectors**, segmentation default-deny, AES-256-GCM encryption with tamper detection, and the audit hash chain (including detecting a tampered entry).
- **End-to-end** (`tests/e2e.ts`): drives the real gateway function — sign-in with 2FA, brute-force lockout, allow/deny decisions, step-up, just-in-time grants, and audit-chain verification.

CI runs typecheck, tests and build on every push (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`).

## Deploy on Netlify

Build command `npm run build`, publish directory `dist`. The functions in `netlify/functions/` and Blobs storage are picked up automatically. Set `TESSERA_KEY` under Site settings → Environment variables.

## License

MIT © 2026 Nishant Singh. A demonstration project; the sandbox data is fictional.

# Tideline

**Stream processing on Wikipedia's live edit stream.** Tideline reads every change made on every Wikimedia wiki, as it happens, and runs Apache Flink-style queries over it in your browser: event-time windows, watermarks, late data, window Top-N, changelogs and pattern matching. It includes a Flink SQL console (or ask in English), a working model of Kafka partitions and consumer groups, and a crash-and-recover demo that shows exactly-once processing. The engine is checked row by row against real Apache Flink.

**Live:** https://tideline-nishant.netlify.app  ·  **Author:** [Nishant Singh](https://nishant-singhaa0240274.netlify.app)

## Features

- **Live.** About 30 changes a second from [Wikimedia EventStreams](https://stream.wikimedia.org/?doc), drawn at the time they happened, with the watermark sweeping across. Dots left behind the line arrived late. Drag the watermark delay and watch the late count change.
  - Live panels: changes per 10-second window by project, trending articles (a window Top-N over a sliding 10-minute window), people and bots, late events by kind and lateness, new articles, big edits, edit wars and dead letters.
  - A diagram of the running job graph with each operator's counters and state size.
- **Flink SQL.** Write queries against the `recentchange` table and they run continuously on the live stream, starting now or replaying from 10 minutes or 1 hour ago.
  - Supported: `TUMBLE`, `HOP`, `CUMULATE` and `SESSION` window table functions, window Top-N, unbounded `GROUP BY` with a retract changelog (`+I`, `-U`, `+U`), `FILTER`, `CASE`, `DISTINCT`, the aggregates and 41 scalar functions.
  - **Show plan** prints a Flink-style `EXPLAIN`. Errors point at the line and column, and read like Flink's.
  - **Ask in English:** Gemini writes the query, and Tideline's own parser compiles it before you see it. If it doesn't compile, the error goes back to the model.
  - **Share** saves a query to a short link.
- **Kafka.** A model of a Kafka topic and consumer group, fed by the live stream.
  - Producing uses Kafka's real partitioner: murmur2 for keyed records, sticky batches without a key.
  - Change the key and see a hot partition (every Wikidata change lands on one).
  - Switch between range, round-robin and cooperative-sticky assignment.
  - Crash a consumer and watch the rebalance and the lag.
  - Under at-most-once, at-least-once or exactly-once delivery, it counts what gets lost or processed twice.
- **Recovery.** Two copies of one job count the stream. The primary checkpoints its state to the server every 15 seconds: Kafka position, watermark, open windows and recently seen ids.
  - Crash it, then recover in one of three ways: restore and replay with deduplication (exactly once), without deduplication (at least once), or from the latest data (at most once).
  - A window-by-window comparison with the reference shows the difference.
- **How it works.** The parity report against Apache Flink, the architecture, and which course each part puts into practice.

## Checked against Apache Flink

The same 26,453 events went through Apache Flink 2.3.0 (PyFlink, local mini-cluster) and through Tideline's engine. **All 18 queries give the same result: 15,010 rows**, including the count of changelog messages and the `MATCH_RECOGNIZE` edit-war matches.

- The settings make Flink's output repeatable: parallelism 1, UTC, and a watermark after every record (`pipeline.auto-watermark-interval = 0`).
- The test data comes from a deterministic generator modelled on the real stream, because the live stream can't be replayed in CI. It includes late category changes and edit wars.
- The check caught two real bugs in Tideline, both now fixed. A window table function used without aggregation was dropping late rows instead of passing them through. The edit-war matcher was forgetting a revert that could still start a match.
- On **Flink 1.20.3**, 17 of the 18 queries give the same result. The exception is a tumbling window with an offset (`TUMBLE(..., INTERVAL '1' MINUTE, INTERVAL '15' SECOND)`): Flink 1.20.3 itself emits only every other window, with lower counts. Flink 2.3.0 and Tideline emit every window, with the same numbers.

```bash
npm test                                      # 167 checks, including parity with the committed Flink results
pip install apache-flink==2.3.0               # needs Java 11+
npm run parity:data && python3 tests/flink/run_flink.py && npm test -- parity   # re-run Flink yourself
```

## The same pipeline on real Kafka and Flink

`pipeline/` runs it for real with Docker Compose. A Python producer reads EventStreams, validates and flattens each event, and produces it to Kafka. The producer is:

- idempotent;
- keyed by wiki with Java-compatible murmur2 partitioning;
- writing Avro, with the schema in Schema Registry;
- backed by a dead-letter topic for events that fail validation.

One Flink SQL job runs the website's queries, generated from the same source file (`shared/queries.ts`). It keeps RocksDB state, checkpoints every 10 s, and writes results back to Kafka exactly once. See [pipeline/README.md](pipeline/README.md).

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  ES[(Wikimedia EventStreamsKafka over SSE)] -->|fetch + SSE parser| W
  subgraph Browser
    W[Web Workervalidate · dedupe · watermarks] --> E[Stream enginewindows · Top-N · changelog · CEP]
    Q[Flink SQLlexer → parser → planner] --> E
    W --> K[Kafka modelpartitioner · assignors · offsets]
    E --> UI[React UI · SVG charts]
  end
  subgraph Netlify
    F["Functions: /api/checkpoints · /api/queries · /api/ai/sql · /api/health"] --> B[(Netlify Blobs)]
    F --> G[Gemini API]
    F --> Q2[same SQL compilervalidates AI output]
  end
  UI <--> F
```

- **`shared/engine/`**: event time and watermarks (bounded out-of-orderness), window assigners, window and group aggregates (with retractions), window Top-N, the edit-war detector (`MATCH_RECOGNIZE` semantics), and snapshot/restore for every operator.
- **`shared/sql/`**: a lexer, a recursive-descent parser for Flink's dialect (431 reserved words), and a planner.
  - The planner type-checks with Flink's rules: integer division, `AVG` of an `INT` is an `INT`, three-valued logic, case-sensitive names.
  - It produces operators (`Calc`, `WindowAggregate`, `GroupAggregate`, `WindowRank`, `Limit`) and an `EXPLAIN` plan.
- **`shared/kafka/`**: Kafka's murmur2 partitioner (checked against the Java client's outputs), plus range, round-robin and cooperative-sticky assignors.
- **`src/worker/`**: the stream client. It reads Wikimedia's SSE wire format with `fetch`, reconnects with `?since=`, and deduplicates by `meta.id`. Every event carries its Kafka topic, partition and offset.

### API

| Method | Path | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/checkpoints` | Store a recovery checkpoint (state snapshot), get an id |
| GET | `/api/checkpoints/:id` | Load it back |
| POST | `/api/queries` | Save a SQL query, get a share id |
| GET | `/api/queries/:id` | A shared query |
| POST | `/api/ai/sql` | Question in English → Flink SQL that compiles, with an explanation |
| GET | `/api/health` | Status and whether AI is configured |

Everything is validated with Zod and rate-limited per visitor. The AI endpoint also has a daily cap to protect the API quota. A daily scheduled function deletes checkpoints older than a day and old rate-limit counters. Shared queries are kept.

## Tech stack

TypeScript everywhere · React 18 + Vite · Web Workers · Netlify Functions (Node 22) · Netlify Blobs · Zod · Gemini API (structured JSON output) · hand-built SVG charts · Python (confluent-kafka, Avro, pytest, PyFlink) · Docker Compose · Apache Kafka (KRaft) · Confluent Schema Registry · Apache Flink · GitHub Actions.

Design: a nautical chart. The page is chart paper with shoal-blue water still "open" for late data, buff land for the control panel, and a magenta tide line for the watermark. Type is Newsreader, Sofia Sans and Fragment Mono.

## Run it yourself

```bash
npm install
npx netlify dev                       # http://localhost:8888, reading the real stream
```

Offline, with a local stand-in for EventStreams (same wire format, `?since=` replay and dropped connections):

```bash
npm run mock                          # http://localhost:8787
VITE_STREAM_URL=http://localhost:8787/v2/stream/recentchange npx netlify dev
```

**Deploy on Netlify:** build command `npm run build`, publish directory `dist`.

| Environment variable | Required | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | No | Enables "Ask in English". Without it, everything else works. |
| `GEMINI_MODEL` | No | Overrides the model choice |
| `DAILY_AI_LIMIT` | No | AI requests per day across all visitors (default 300) |

## Tests

| Command | What it checks |
|---|---|
| `npm test` | 167 checks: window firing at `watermark >= window_end - 1`, every window type, changelogs, Top-N, time zones, checkpoint → crash → restore giving exactly-once results, edit-war matching, SQL parsing, typing and errors, three-valued logic, murmur2 against Kafka's Java client, the assignors, and the parity with Flink |
| `python3 tests/api_test.py` | 20 end-to-end API checks against `netlify dev` with a mock Gemini (`tests/mock_gemini.py`): checkpoints, shared queries, AI retries with the parser's error, unanswerable questions, rate limits |
| `cd pipeline/producer && pytest` | The Kafka producer, on librdkafka's mock cluster and a mock Schema Registry |
| `python3 pipeline/flink/check_sql.py` | The pipeline's Flink job, planned and run by Flink itself |
| `npm run typecheck` | Strict TypeScript |

CI runs all of them on every push (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`), with Flink 1.20.3 and 2.3.0.

## Limits

- The browser engine runs with parallelism 1 and keeps state in memory. It's for learning and demonstrating the semantics, not a replacement for Flink.
- Wikimedia's stream resumes from a timestamp, not an exact offset, so recovery replays a little overlap and relies on deduplication by event id.
- The Docker Compose stack wasn't started in the environment this was built in (no container runtime). Its SQL is validated by Flink's planner and its producer by tests.

## License

Code: MIT © 2026 Nishant Singh. Live data: [Wikimedia EventStreams](https://wikitech.wikimedia.org/wiki/Event_Platform/EventStreams_HTTP_Service). Wikimedia content is available under [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/).

# TOUCHLINE — Match Intelligence

A free-first, multi-page football analysis prototype for Vercel. Pages work in demo mode without credentials:

- `index.html` — match room, sample event timeline, rule-based tactical prompts, country-aware official streaming link.
- `dream-league.html` — editable player lineups, CSV import/template download, explainable matchup probabilities, animated five-minute mini-match.
- `clips.html` — search official YouTube-published clips, with a direct YouTube fallback when no API key is configured; regional streaming destination.
- `method.html` — model notes, limitations, sources, and setup information.

## Deploy on Vercel

1. Upload the contents of this folder to a GitHub repository.
2. In Vercel, import that repository. No build command or framework preset is needed; leave the output directory at the project root.
3. Deploy. Demo mode works immediately.
4. Optional: in **Project → Settings → Environment Variables**, add `API_FOOTBALL_KEY` and/or `YOUTUBE_API_KEY`, then redeploy. These values are read only by serverless functions under `/api`; never put them in browser code.

# TutorMind

**Photograph your handwritten work in any subject. Get it marked, with mistakes explained and mastery tracked.**

TutorMind reads a student's handwritten answers with a vision AI, marks each answer against the question and a reference, explains the *type* of mistake, and keeps a record of mastery per subject. Subjects: Maths, English (Lit + Grammar), History, Geography, Hindi, and Other.

---

## How it works

1. **Transcribe first** — the AI writes out what it read from your photo, shown back to you as *"what I read"* so a misread never silently becomes a wrong mark.
2. **Mark against the reference** — using the question paper plus either a **book name + live web search** (free) or an **uploaded reference PDF** (Pro).
3. **Explain** — per-answer feedback and the mistake type.
4. **Track mastery** — saved on the device, shown on the Progress page.

Grading runs in a serverless function (`/api/grade`) that calls **Google Gemini** (multimodal — it reads images and PDFs). The key stays server-side.

---

## Free vs Pro

| | Free | Pro (unlock code) |
|---|---|---|
| Subjects | all | all |
| Answer pages | 1 per paper | multiple |
| Reference | book name + web search | + upload your own PDF |
| Gradings / day | 3 | unlimited |

Pro is the heavy, token-hungry path (PDF grounding, multi-page), which is why it's gated. Default unlock code: **`TUTORMIND-PRO-2026`** (change `PRO_CODE` in `practice.html`).

---

## Pages

```
tutormind/
├── index.html      # Home
├── practice.html   # The grader (subject, question, reference, answer photos)
├── progress.html   # Mastery per subject (stored on device)
├── how.html        # Method + honest limits
├── style.css       # Shared Graph Paper styling
├── api/
│   └── grade.js    # Serverless → Gemini vision grading
└── README.md
```

---

## Deploying to Vercel (free)

1. Push this folder to a GitHub repo.
2. Vercel: **Add New → Project → Import** → Framework **Other**, build settings empty.
3. Get a free Gemini key at **[Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/app/apikey)**.
4. Vercel → **Settings → Environment Variables** → add `GEMINI_API_KEY` = your key (Production + Preview).
5. Deploy. Vercel auto-detects `api/grade.js`.

The grader only runs on the deployed site (where the key + function exist). In a local/static preview, use **"See a sample result"**. Image downscaling, uploads, and the UI work everywhere.

---

## Honest limits

- **Handwriting reading is imperfect**, especially messy writing and **Hindi / Devanagari** — always check the transcription.
- **It does not download textbooks** — that would be copyright infringement, and no legitimate free API does it. Free grading uses the book *name* + web search; upload a chapter you're allowed to use for exact grounding (Pro).
- **Whole textbooks are too large** for the free tier (hard request-size + token limits). Use a chapter or a few pages. The client caps uploads at ~4.2 MB to stay within Vercel's request limit.
- **Essay/literature marks are subjective** — treat as structured feedback, not an official grade.
- Free Gemini is rate-limited; grading uses a lot per request, so you may hit limits — wait a minute, or use Pro.

---

## Configuration

- **Models:** `MODELS` in `api/grade.js` (Flash-Lite → Flash → newest). The first your key can use without quota wins.
- **Limits / code:** `CONFIG` at the top of `practice.html`.

---

*A study aid, not a substitute for your teacher. Your mastery record stays on your device.*

# VerifyAI

**Check a claim or image before you share it — a verdict with the evidence, powered by live web search.**

VerifyAI is a multi-page web app that fact-checks a statement against the live web and returns a plain verdict (True / Misleading / False / Unverified) with a confidence figure and the **sources it used**. For images, it reads hidden EXIF metadata in your browser and gives one-tap reverse-image search. It's free, with no accounts.

---

## How it works

- **Claims** are sent to a small serverless function (`/api/verify`) which calls **Google Gemini** with **Google Search grounding** — real web search — and returns a structured verdict plus the source links.
- **Images** are read **in your browser** with `exifr` (capture date, camera, editing software, GPS). The image itself is never uploaded. Reverse-image links (Google Lens, TinEye, Bing) help you find where a photo first appeared.

The AI key lives **server-side only**, as an environment variable — it is never exposed to visitors.

---

## Pages

```
verifyai/
├── index.html      # Home (masthead, verdict stamp, method)
├── verify.html     # The verifier (claim + image → verdict + sources)
├── how.html        # How the method works
├── about.html      # About, limits, honest disclaimers
├── style.css       # Shared Editorial Newsroom styling
├── api/
│   └── verify.js   # Serverless function → Gemini + Google Search
└── README.md
```

Every page links to the others through the top navigation.

---

## Deploying to Vercel (free)

1. Push this whole folder to a GitHub repo.
2. In Vercel: **Add New → Project → Import** the repo. Framework preset: **Other**. Leave build settings empty.
3. **Get a free Gemini API key:** go to **[Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/app/apikey)** → *Create API key*. (Free tier, no card.)
4. In Vercel → your project → **Settings → Environment Variables**, add:
   - **Name:** `GEMINI_API_KEY`
   - **Value:** *(your key)*
   - Apply to Production (and Preview).
5. **Deploy** (or redeploy after adding the key). Your site is live at `https://<your-project>.vercel.app/`.

The `/api/verify` function runs automatically — Vercel detects the `api/` folder; no extra config needed.

> **Note:** the verifier only returns real results on the deployed Vercel site (where the key and the serverless function exist). In a static/local preview, the backend isn't running — use the **"See a sample verdict"** button to preview the result UI. Image EXIF and reverse-image links work everywhere.

### Netlify instead?
Netlify works too, but the function path differs (`netlify/functions/verify.js` + a redirect from `/api/verify`). Vercel is the simplest for this layout.

---

## Cost

- **Gemini API** has a free tier that comfortably covers personal/demo use. If you exceed it, Google may require billing — monitor usage in Google AI Studio.
- **Vercel Hobby** hosting and serverless functions are free for personal projects.

No other paid services are used.

---

## Configuration

- **Model:** change `MODEL` at the top of `api/verify.js` (default `gemini-2.5-flash`).
- **Prompt / verdict rules:** edit the prompt string in `api/verify.js`.
- **Sample claims / demo result:** edit `SAMPLES` and `DEMO` in `verify.html`.

---

## Honest limitations

VerifyAI uses an AI model with web search. It can be confidently wrong, miss context, or rely on a weak source. It is a **starting point**, not a final authority — always open the sources and judge them yourself. It can't fact-check opinions or predictions, struggles with breaking news (expect "Unverified"), and can't prove an image is AI-generated (metadata is a hint, not proof). It is **not a substitute for professional fact-checking**.

---

*Free, no account. Your images never leave your device.*

# Batchline — Micro-producer traceability workbench

Batchline links ingredient lots to small production runs, quality notes, and trade dispatches. The workflow is designed for a one-to-ten-person producer who needs to answer “which batches used this lot?” and “where did that batch go?” without maintaining a complex enterprise system.

## Run and deploy

This is a static site. Open `index.html` directly or deploy this folder to Vercel with no build command and no environment variables. Three.js and GSAP load from public CDNs for the mixing-vessel scene and entrance motion. If Three.js is unavailable, an inline illustrated vessel is used. No paid service or API key is required.

## What works in the browser demo

- Eight connected pages cover overview, ingredient lots, production runs, trace and recall exercises, dispatch, quality checks, suppliers, and records.
- Ingredient lots, production runs, dispatch notes, quality checks, supplier records, and activity are saved to this browser's local storage.
- Recording a production run deducts the entered quantities from selected ingredient lots and creates a bidirectional lot-to-batch trace link.
- Dispatch notes link a batch to a trade destination and quantity. A trace view shows connected dispatches without storing end-customer names or contact details.
- A mock trace exercise computes connected batches and sample dispatches from local records. It does not send recall messages.
- Quality logs and manually entered release states are stored locally. The app does not determine food safety or compliance.
- Archive metadata can be exported as JSON, restored from JSON, and quality logs as CSV. No data is sent anywhere unless you export and share it.
- Starter records and trade destinations are fictional examples for Thane. They are not verified suppliers, businesses, recipes, food-safety checks, or actual transactions.

## Scope and limits

This is a portfolio prototype, not a food-safety certification or a complete production system. It has no user accounts, shared database, cloud sync, sensor or POS connections, supplier verification, customer notifications, or AI model. Browser storage is device-specific and is not an encrypted long-term archive. Labels such as “Released” are operator-entered demo states. Review your food-safety processes with qualified people before using any production system for real operations.

Food traceability already has established software products, including systems aimed at smaller producers. Batchline explores a narrower, low-friction workflow for micro-producers rather than claiming the general category is untouched.

## Files

- `index.html` — app shell and eight-page navigation
- `styles.css` — dark stainless-and-citrus visual system, responsive layout
- `app.js` — local data model, trace paths, forms, and Three.js vessel scene
- `FEATURES.md` — capability inventory and demo boundaries

# ChurnLens — keep the revenue you already have

Winning a customer costs ~5× keeping one — yet most teams find out about churn in the cancellation email. **ChurnLens** scores every account with a real risk model, explains exactly *why* each one is at risk, maps retention cohorts, and lets you **simulate retention plays against real MRR** before you spend a dollar. Everything runs in the browser.

## Run it
Open `index.html`, or `python3 -m http.server 8080`. No build, no dependencies, fully offline.

## Pages
- **Home** — pitch + a live 3D cohort-decay ribbon hero (retention survival curves).
- **Customers** — all 40 accounts scored and ranked by churn risk; search, filter by band, sort. Click one for a drawer showing its **explainable risk factors** and the recommended retention play.
- **Cohorts** — a monthly **retention triangle** (heatmap of % retained by cohort × month) and overlaid survival curves.
- **Segments** — where churn concentrates: average risk and MRR-at-risk by plan and by region.
- **Simulator** — four retention levers (engagement, price, NPS, proactive support), each changing a feature the model actually uses; it **re-scores all 40 accounts live** and shows accounts saved, annual revenue retained, and a before/after retention curve.
- **Settings** — theme, accents, JSON export.

## The model is real
A logistic churn model (`churnProb`) over six features — tenure, engagement, support friction, NPS, price sensitivity and plan tier — each with a signed weight. Risk is `sigmoid(w·features)`. The customer drawer decomposes the score into **per-factor contributions** (a SHAP-style explanation), and the simulator recomputes the whole book by adjusting features and re-running the same model — so the revenue numbers move for a real reason.

## Deploy
Static — Netlify drop, `vercel`, or GitHub Pages.

## Feature count
50+ — risk scoring, explainable factors, risk bands, cohort retention triangle, survival curves, segment analysis, MRR at risk, what-if simulator with live re-scoring, revenue impact, 3D hero, theming, export, offline. Full list on the home page.

*The real market need: SaaS teams react to churn instead of predicting it (cf. retention/CS tooling). ChurnLens is a self-contained demonstration of predictive churn + retention simulation.*
